notes.signature: Radar signature (docs/REFERENCE.md 9.2). rcs_shape: an ESTIMATE from this repo's geometry, not RCS data (none is public) -- generated by tools/fit/rcs_shape.py. The mean RCS seen from a direction is the airframe's projected area in that direction (the optical-region RCS of a large sphere is exactly its projected area), with the airframe as four body-axis ellipsoids: fuselage (length = hit box 49.3 ft; depth = intake lip to eyepoint, 66.1 in; half-width = mean of the ventral-fin and main-gear stations, 36.4 in -- f16.xml structure points), wing (span 30 ft and area 300 ft2 from f16.xml metrics), horizontal tail (63.7 ft2; span from an ESTIMATED aspect ratio 3.0, the wing's) and fin (54.75 ft2; height 93.7 in from fin tip to eyepoint level); thickness/chord 0.04 for every surface, an ESTIMATE. It gives 3.8 m2 nose-on (inside the ~1-5 m2 of open-literature frontal estimates for the type), 25.4 m2 beam-on, 55.8 m2 from above or below. No specular flashes, inlet/nozzle cavities or edge diffraction: a real fighter is spikier than its silhouette. The nose-on value is the type's static RCS, which a scenario's radar_cross_section.static_rcs_m2 rescales. fluctuation_model swerling_1: an exponentially distributed return, independent each sweep -- Fehlner (APL Technical Digest, 1963): observed aircraft data agree with Swerling Cases 1 and 2. No fighter-specific RCS statistics were found.
notes.rwr: AN/ALR-56M class. sensitivity_dbm -65: the typical RWR sensitivity in NAWCWD TP 8347, Electronic Warfare and Radar Systems Engineering Handbook (Receiver Sensitivity / Noise). No ALR-56M figure is public (FAS gives the architecture only). antenna_gain 1 (0 dBi): ESTIMATE -- RWR antennas are broad-beam spirals/cavities near 0 dBi; no source found. The link receives the illuminator's peak power. A 20 dBi antenna with a threshold solved for 90 nmi would be ~11 dB less sensitive than the handbook's typical figure. signal_jitter_db 0 and sweep_period_s 0.5: ESTIMATES -- no jitter on the received power (the radar's own Swerling fluctuation is not on this one-way path), and a sweep twice as fast as the 1 s radar sweep it listens to.
notes.radar: AN/APG-68. No APG-68 transmitter, receiver or waveform figure is public; see docs/REFERENCE.md 9.8 and docs/SOURCES.md (Radar). average_power_w 200 and peak_power_w 20000: the APG-66 family's figures (Forecast International, APG-66(V), 2003 -- quoted for the SASS variant, used as the family's transmitter estimate). antenna_gain 2000 (33.0 dBi): inside the 32.9-34.3 dBi that the F-16 radar's 75.3 x 48.8 cm planar array gives at 50-70 % aperture efficiency (same source). frequency_hz 9.86e9: Wikipedia, AN/APG-68. noise_figure_db 4: ESTIMATE, mid-range of a 3-5 dB system figure over ~1.5 dB X-band LNAs. time_on_target_s 0.047: a ~2.8 deg beam (1.2 lambda/D) swept at 60 deg/s, the APG-66's antenna scan rate (US Patent 4,673,938). frame_time_s 4.4: one +/-60 deg, 2-bar search frame, 2 x (120 deg / 60 deg/s + 0.2 s turnaround) -- the rates from the same patent, the 2-bar volume an ESTIMATE; every target in the cone gets one look per frame. stt_frame_time_s 0.1: ESTIMATE, no published single-target-track update rate was found; 10 Hz, at the slow end of how fire-control trackers are described, so a lock costs little per tick. In STT the radar looks only at the locked target, once per STT frame, with the same per-look budget as a search look (no extended STT dwell is modelled). confirm_frames 3 of confirm_window_frames 5: track confirmation at 3 of 5 frames ('three or more scans are usually necessary to establish a valid track', Fundamentals of Naval Weapons Systems ch. 6). drop_frames 3: ESTIMATE, a confirmed track drops after 3 frames (~13 s) with no detection. stt_drop_frames 10: ESTIMATE, a lock breaks after 10 STT frames (1 s) with no detection; 3 frames (0.3 s) broke a lock every ~4 s at launch range, where one look detects about half the time, because each look here gets a scan look's budget and a fresh Swerling 1 draw. fire_control_delay_s 3.0: ESTIMATE, the midpoint of the patent's 'acceptable fire-control delay' of 2-4 s at long range. pfa 1e-6: design convention; it sets the square-law search threshold, ln(1/pfa) = 11.40 dB over noise. system_loss_db 7.9630: FITTED, the only free budget parameter -- CALIBRATED by tools/fit/radar_budget.py so one look at a Swerling 1 5 m2 reference target (no aspect factor) detects with probability 0.5 at the cited 50 nmi, in free space (the sim models no atmospheric absorption, so the air's ~0.4 dB at that range is inside L). Total losses of 8-10 dB are typical (MIT Lincoln Laboratory, O'Donnell 2002): 7.96 dB is just below that range, so the cited 50 nmi asks slightly more of this hardware than is typical -- a recorded discrepancy, not tuned away (docs/VALIDATION.md, Where it is weakest). Nose-on against this type's own shape estimate (3.78 m2) the same radar detects at 46.6 nmi. antenna_height_m 0.488: the 48.8 cm height of the 75.3 x 48.8 cm array (Forecast International). The Doppler notch applies only while the beam, one elevation beamwidth (beamwidth_factor x lambda / antenna_height_m, 4.28 deg) either side of the line of sight, touches the 4/3-Earth surface: main-beam clutter is ground lit by the main beam (MIT Lincoln Laboratory, O'Donnell 2002, MTI and Pulse Doppler Processing), so looking up with sky behind the whole beam a beaming target has no clutter to hide in (docs/REFERENCE.md 9.3). Reach of one beamwidth: ESTIMATE, the strong part of the main lobe (a tapered aperture's first null sits ~1.25 beamwidths out). Track measurement (docs/REFERENCE.md 9.11): each detection measures range and two angles with errors ~ resolution / sqrt(SNR) (MIT Lincoln Laboratory, Parameter Estimation and Tracking). antenna_width_m 0.753: the array's 75.3 cm width (Forecast International). beamwidth_factor 1.2: ESTIMATE, a tapered aperture's half-power beamwidth 1.2 lambda/D, recalled -> 2.78 x 4.28 deg. monopulse_slope 1.6: classic monopulse form, recalled; reproduces Lincoln Laboratory's 10:1 beam splitting at ~13 dB. pulse_width_s 1e-6: ESTIMATE inside the APG-66(V)2's published 0.81-4 us; no pulse-compression figure is public. track_maneuver_g 3: ESTIMATE, the Kalman tracker's 1-sigma allowance for target acceleration; no source. The datalink relays this track to the missile.
notes.jsbsim_model: JSBSim's F-16A Block 32 model, rebuilt for the F-16C: drag refitted to NASA TP-3414 (flight) and TP-3355 (tunnel), Mach-dependent lift, a designed load-factor pitch FCS (tools/drivers/fcs_identify + fcs_design.py), and F100-PW-229 thrust fitted to this type's flight manual (tools/drivers/drag_sample + thrust_fit.py). See docs/REFERENCE.md 4.1.
notes.wing_area_ft2: The flight model's own reference area (metrics/Sw-sqft); published 300 ft2.
notes.hit_box_ft: 30 ft span (the flight model's metric, not the wingtip-rail figure some specifications quote), 16.7 ft height, 49.3 ft length.
notes.cl_max: Lift at the ~25 deg 1 g AoA limit, measured quasi-statically on the flight model (NASA TP-1538 tables) with the leading-edge flaps scheduled down; the FCS's AoA limiter holds the same angle. Scaled in flight by the model's aero/function/kCLmax-mach.
notes.structural_g_limit: +9 / -3 G: USAF F-16 fact sheet; the FCS commands at most 9 G.
notes.damage: Overstress damage rate, not aircraft data: ESTIMATE, sized so a brief modest overstress accrues a small fraction of the failure threshold (damage 1.0 = 100 G-s over the limit). See docs/REFERENCE.md 5.
notes.flight_controls: The pitch FCS reads the stick as a load-factor command, 8 G per unit of aft stick on top of 1 G. The throttle command passes a gain-of-2 stage before JSBSim's 0-2 throttle position, so 0.5 is military power and 1.0 full afterburner.
notes.fuel: Tanks named 'internal left/right' (3 486 lb each); 'external station 4/6' are drop tanks.
notes.reference: reference/ holds the F-16C flight manual's data (T.O. GR1F-16CJ-1-1, Appendix A) used to fit and validate this type.
notes.cl_max_loss_per_g: The F-16 FLCS's G/AoA blend: the AoA it allows falls with load factor. The flight manual's quickest turn at sea level (24.8 deg/s at 9 G, 22 000 lb, T.O. GR1F-16CJ-1-1) needs CL 1.26 at 9 G against 1.65 at 1 g: (1.65 - 1.26) / 8 = 0.049 per G. The flight model's limiter (fcs/alpha-limit-deg, 21 - 0.8 (Nz - 1) deg) gives the same lift; both are calibrated to the quickest turns.
